slides.title: Why do your blades rust in the bag?
slides.sub: Guards and soakers do two different jobs

slides.title: Water is the real enemy
slides.body: A thin film of melted ice left on ground steel inside a closed bag is all it takes to start pitting an edge.

slides.title: Guards are for walking
slides.body: Fit hard guards the moment you step off the ice. One unguarded step onto a hard floor can nick an edge.

slides.title: Two covers, two different jobs
slides.caption: Guards handle the walk, soakers handle the bag.

slides.title: The 90 second routine
slides.body: Guards on at the barrier, boots off, guards off and wipe the whole blade dry, let the steel air, then soakers on for the bag.

slides.title: Dry the soakers at home
slides.body: Pull the soakers off and let blades and soakers dry fully. A permanently damp soaker holds moisture against the steel.

slides.title: Read the rust stage
slides.body: Grey haze wipes off with a dry cloth. Orange speckling needs a light stone that week. Pitting on the running surface needs a technician.
